### Day 39: 1 Samuel 31:1–13
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-39-1-samuel-31-113.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 31:11-12
Points:
- The Philistines desecrated Saul's body by impaling it on the wall of Beth-shan.
- Men of valor from Jabesh-gilead marched all night at great personal risk to rescue the bodies of Saul and his sons.
- Their heroic devotion stemmed from remembering Saul's rescue of their town over forty years earlier.
- Gratitude should not expire with time; believers ought to keep long memories for kindness and short memories for offenses.
- God's faithful servants are those who remember His deliverance and honor debts of love.

### Your Epitaph - Today's Insight - January 10, 2024
Author: Chuck Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/todays-insight-january-10-2024.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 31:11-13
Points:
- Saul's burial under the tamarisk tree serves as a sorrowful epitaph to a wasted potential.
- Death is inevitable for all people, requiring everyone to face mortality honestly.
- While the earthly body decays and passes away, Christians possess an inward spirit renewed by Christ.
- Facing mortality prompts believers to examine the authenticity and legacy of their daily walk.
